chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Subah, from one of our companions, who said:

Al-Rabi' came to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur while he was performing the circumambulation (al-Tawaf). He said to him, 'O Commander of the Faithful, so-and-so, your mawla, died last night, and so-and-so cut off his head after his death.' He became furious and angry. He said to Ibn Shubrumah, Ibn Abi Layla, and a number of judges and jurists with him, 'What do you say about this?' Each of them said, 'We have nothing regarding this.' He kept repeating the question regarding this, saying, 'Shall I kill him or not?' They said, 'We have nothing regarding this.'

He said, 'One of them said to him, 'A man has arrived at this moment; if anyone has something regarding this, the answer is with him, and he is Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and he has entered into al-Mas'a.' So he said to al-Rabi', 'Go to him and say to him, 'Had we not known of your preoccupation with what you are in, we would have asked you to come to us, but answer us regarding such and such.'

He said, 'So al-Rabi' came to him while he was at al-Marwa, and he delivered the message to him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'You see the preoccupation I am in, and the jurists and scholars are before you, so ask them.' He said to him, 'I have asked them, and there was nothing with them regarding it.' He said, 'So he returned him to him and said, 'I ask you, do not answer us regarding it, for the people have nothing regarding this.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Until I finish from what I am in.'

He said, 'So when he finished, he came and sat by the side of the Sacred Mosque. He said to al-Rabi', 'Go and say to him, 'Upon him is one hundred dinars.' He said, 'So he delivered that to him. They said to him, 'Ask him how it became one hundred dinars upon him.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'In the nutfah (seed/drop) is twenty, and in the 'alaqah (clot) is twenty, and in the mudghah (lump) is twenty, and in the 'izam (bones) is twenty, and in the lahm (flesh) is twenty. Then We developed it into another creation, and this is a dead person in the status of what it was before the soul was blown into it in the belly of its mother, a fetus.'

He said, 'So he returned to him and informed him of the answer. They were amazed by that and said, 'Return to him and ask him about the dinars, for whom are they? For his heirs or not?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'There is nothing for his heirs in it. Rather, this is something that came to him in his body after his death. It is used to perform Hajj on his behalf, or to give charity on his behalf, or it becomes in a way from the ways of goodness.'

He said, 'The man claimed that they sent the messenger back to him, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) answered regarding it with thirty-six questions, and the man did not memorize except to the extent of this answer.'

key_terms.الْمَسْعَى: Al-Mas'a (The area between Safa and Marwa)

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a person decapitated after death according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential superiority of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) over the Abbasid judicial establishment, as he resolved a novel case of 'post-mortem mutilation' (qatl ba'd al-mawt) that stumped the caliph's jurists. By linking the compensation to the five stages of fetal development, the Imam established a precise metaphysical valuation of the body's potential for life, treating the decapitated corpse as a fetus before the soul's infusion. The ruling that the *diyah* is not inherited but spent on the deceased's behalf underscores the Shia view of posthumous spiritual benefits and distinguishes this specific compensation from standard inheritance laws.
